# Indian Philosophy — Differentiation, Emptiness, Manifestation, Recognition

The Indian line in *The Return of Zero* contains several arguments that meet without becoming one doctrine. Sāṃkhya distinguishes the experient from an articulated inner instrument. Buddhist philosophy makes dependent arising and exclusion central to the formation of things and concepts. Indian mathematics gives *śūnya* explicit arithmetic work. Kashmir Śaivism asks how undivided consciousness can manifest a genuinely differentiated world and recognise itself through that differentiation. The essay draws these lines together around one pressure: a world becomes determinate through operations that no finished determination contains by itself.

## Sāṃkhya: the subject and the inner instrument

The [*Sāṃkhya Kārikā* in the Colebrooke/Wilson carrier](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/isvarakrishna/isvarakrishna-colebrooke-wilson-1837-sankhya-karika/isvarakrishna-colebrooke-wilson-1837-sankhya-karika.md) supplies an early functional discrimination among *buddhi*, *ahaṃkāra*, and *manas*: determination, appropriation under the form of I and mine, and coordination among presentations and alternatives. These belong to *prakṛti*'s articulated apparatus. *Puruṣa* occupies a different position as witness or experient. [§0 · #1](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/08-s0-p1-inner-instrument.md) inherits this distinction because it prevents the contents and machinery of an interior world from being mistaken for the pole to which that world appears. The later agentic comparison depends on exactly this historical achievement: model, memory, policy, self-description, and attention can be richly organised while remaining describable functions within objective internality.

## Buddhist lines: dependent arising, emptiness, and exclusion

[Nāgārjuna's *Fundamental Wisdom of the Middle Way*](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/nagarjuna/nagarjuna-garfield-1995-fundamental-wisdom/nagarjuna-garfield-1995-fundamental-wisdom.md) gives emptiness its dependent force: phenomena lack isolated self-subsistence because they arise through conditions. Ground therefore names the field of relations through which a phenomenon arises and acts, rather than a second self-grounding substance placed behind it. That current enters [§0 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/09-s0-p2-vikalpa-samkalpa.md), where *pratītya-samutpāda* gives an ontogenic form to world-making, and [§2 · #0](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/19-s2-p0-difference-cannot-be-escaped.md), where nonduality must preserve real differentiation inside conditioned appearance.

Dignāga's later semantic work makes the cut precise in language. [Ole Holten Pind's study and translations of *anyāpoha*](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/pind/pind-2009-dignaga-anyapoha-dissertation/pind-2009-dignaga-anyapoha-dissertation.md) carries the claim that a word expresses its own referent through exclusion of other referents. The second passage in the same house blocks an easy reduction to bare negation: the referent is treated as a thing qualified by preclusion, while the fragment's attribution remains philologically qualified. [§0/1 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/00-integral-threshold/movements/03-s01-p2-definition-cut-gift-danger.md) first uses this to show definition as a productive cut; [§0 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/10-s0-p3-apoha.md) then follows exclusion into the field it retains. The edited volume [*Apoha: Buddhist Nominalism and Human Cognition*](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/siderits/siderits-tillemans-chakrabarti-2011-apoha/siderits-tillemans-chakrabarti-2011-apoha.md) marks the wider scholarly argument still to be worked chapter by chapter.

The tetralemma's modern formal afterlife now belongs to this history as well. [Priest's open-access study](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/priest/priest-2010-logic-catuskoti/priest-2010-logic-catuskoti.md) and [*The Fifth Corner of Four*](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/priest/priest-2018-fifth-corner/priest-2018-fifth-corner.md) read the catuṣkoṭi through First Degree Entailment, whose four values are the subsets of {T, F} — four relational positions generated from two marks. When Nāgārjuna rejects all four corners, Priest adds a fifth status, ineffability, that sits outside the lattice and infects whatever contains it; at the ultimate level only that status remains, so the conventional exhausts the four corners while the ultimate lives beyond them. The instructive limit is that his fifth value is inert — nothing in the value-theory returns from it — while the tradition itself performs the return the formalism cannot write: Jizang's hierarchy iterates the two truths so that each level's conventional/ultimate pair becomes the next level's conventional; the Vimalakīrti's silence resolves by performance; Dōgen returns the ultimate to the ordinary. [§3 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/04-mathematical-substrate/movements/28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing.md) takes the structure as the essay's strongest external neighbour for the sixfold count and states its own reading — the four corners as an unrecognised internal `#1–#4`, the silent fifth as ground-analogue, the practised return as the missing `5→0` — as Argued, under the gates of [Garfield and Priest's limits-of-thought paper](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/garfield/garfield-priest-2003-limits-of-thought/garfield-priest-2003-limits-of-thought.md), [Kapsner's rejection of the fifth value](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/kapsner/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners.md), and the Buddhological objections carried in the source houses. That the completion of this logic is an operation rather than a proposition bears on why the East holds it as lived practice — philosophy as technē — and why its structure could remain implicit yet persistently indicated across the tradition's history.

Śrīharṣa belongs to another Indian debate. [Nilanjan Das's scholarly account](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/das/das-2022-sriharsa-sep/das-2022-sriharsa-sep.md) reports the contention that an awareness cannot present one object as distinct from another without also presenting them as non-distinct. [§2 · #0](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/19-s2-p0-difference-cannot-be-escaped.md) uses that pressure at a narrow point: distinction and non-distinction can be co-given. The section does not turn this into a denial of practical difference; it lets the inherited problem sharpen the two possible accountings of a relation.

## Śūnya enters arithmetic

Indian mathematics gives the history a material pivot. [Colebrooke's 1817 translation of Brahmagupta and Bhāskara](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/brahmagupta/colebrooke-1817-brahmagupta-bhaskara/colebrooke-1817-brahmagupta-bhaskara.md) carries rules for zero among positive and negative quantities and preserves Bhāskara's zero-denominator expressions. [Dutta's 2023 reconstruction](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/dutta/dutta-2023-zero-divided-numbers-india/dutta-2023-zero-divided-numbers-india.md) shows how those expressions can inhabit a changed algebraic regime in which cancellation and cross-multiplication are restricted. [§1 · #1](../../../../../section-rooms/02-return-of-zero/movements/14-s1-p1-sunya-operational.md) therefore learns *śūnya* through what it is allowed to do. Additive identity, multiplicative absorption, and the zero denominator are separate operations, each revealing a different relation between the empty place and the rules of its mathematical world.

## Kashmir Śaivism: manifestation as self-differentiation

The Śaiva stream turns from conditioned things and semantic exclusion toward the manifestation of a whole field. The [*Spandakārikā* source house](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/kallata/spandakarika-dyczkowski-1992-stanzas-vibration/spandakarika-dyczkowski-1992-stanzas-vibration.md) identifies the primary textual corpus and its four commentaries. [Dyczkowski's *Doctrine of Vibration*](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration.md) gives the present source pool its most developed teaching. *Prakāśa* names the luminosity through which things appear; *vimarśa* names consciousness's power of self-apprehension, discrimination, conjunction, and disjunction; *spanda* names the subtle activity through which motion and rest, unity and diversity, manifestation and withdrawal presuppose one another.

Dyczkowski's transcribed pages make the historical operation unusually clear. Reflective awareness differentiates jar from cloth, subject from object, and one level of manifestation from another while remaining one power of awareness. It can divide, hold together, and unite. The movement runs vertically as manifestation and withdrawal, and horizontally as attention moving toward and away from an object. [§0 · #0](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/07-s0-p0-awareness-bends-display.md) receives the reflexive bend; [§0 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/09-s0-p2-vikalpa-samkalpa.md) receives the differentiating and composing pulse; [§0 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/11-s0-p4-tattvic-compression.md) follows the contraction into a situated world.

[Abhinavagupta's *Parātrīśikā-vivaraṇa*](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/abhinavagupta/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana.md) carries the line into Parā Vāk, relational personhood, manifestation, and recognition. The source house carefully separates Jaideva Singh's introduction from Abhinavagupta's commentary and preserves Frank's page-marked leads on Word, communication, and the shared *aham*-field. The thirty-six tattvas then provide the full anatomy: luminosity and power, subjectward and objectward emphasis, the Māyā-produced partition, contracted agency and knowledge, the inner instrument, faculties, and elements, followed by *pratyabhijñā*, recognition within the finite life. [§0 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/11-s0-p4-tattvic-compression.md) compresses this movement so the essay can carry its turns without replacing the full system.

The three Indian lines meet most fruitfully through difference. Sāṃkhya gives a discriminated apparatus and witness; Buddhist philosophy empties determinations of self-subsistence and explains conceptual formation through exclusion; Śaivism describes difference as the self-manifestation and contraction of consciousness. Their historical arguments remain distinct. The essay's process grammar in [§5→0 · #1](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/44-s50-p1-ql-mef-bimba-harness.md) becomes cross-civilisational precisely because it has learned different operations from each rather than converting them into one perennial vocabulary.
